# zust

[![CI](https://github.com/mizchi/zust/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/mizchi/zust/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![Benchmark](https://github.com/mizchi/zust/actions/workflows/bench.yml/badge.svg)](https://mizchi.github.io/zust/dev/bench/)

English | [日本語](README.ja.md)

**zustc** is a compiler for a subset of Rust built for fast incremental builds. **zust-analyzer** is a lightweight LSP server.

- **zustc** has its own front end: lexer, parser and type inference. It generates code with Cranelift (the default) or
  minclif, its own small x86-64 backend. It is tuned for the edit-one-thing-and-rebuild loop of development, and tries
  to minimize:
  - rebuild time
  - peak memory
  - disk used by the cache
  - output binary size

  zustc can compile itself.
- **zust-analyzer** is an LSP server for editors. It answers definition, references, hover, completion, rename and more
  with a light analysis over the token stream and a table of definitions. It works on ordinary Rust workspaces, and
  also indexes std and dependency crates.

> **Status**: experimental.
>
> - zustc only targets Linux x86-64 and does not support all of Rust ([supported language](docs/language.md)).
> - zustc's checks (types, borrow checking without region errors) are partial, so it is not a replacement for rustc for checking correctness.
> - zust-analyzer implements only part of what rust-analyzer does.

## How fast

### Against rustc

Measured with `python3 bench/vs_rustc.py` and `python3 cratebench/run.py` (2026-11-18, 4 cores, rustc 1.100.0; times are
medians of 3 runs). They are measured again with each round of work. gen1000 is a generated program with 1000 functions:

| gen1000 | cold | no-op | edit one function | on disk | binary (stripped) | run |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| zustc | 123 ms | 18 ms | 27 ms | 766 KiB | 324 KiB | 11 ms |
| zustc `-O` | 374 ms | 68 ms | 67 ms | 1199 KiB | 341 KiB | 3 ms |
| rustc `-C incremental` | 756 ms | 197 ms | 406 ms | 10.8 MiB | 1038 KiB | 7 ms |
| rustc `-O` | 18345 ms | - | - | - | 377 KiB | 2 ms |
| **zustc vs rustc `-C incremental`** | **6.1x faster** | **11x faster** | **15x faster** | **14x smaller** | **3.2x smaller** | |

Small programs (`bench/rt`: fib, hashmap, matmul, nbody, sieve, sort, strings) and real crates (cratebench: fnv,
adler2, hex, itoa, rustc-hash, cfg-if; all six give the same output as rustc):

|---|---:|---:|
| cold build | 2.5–4.0x faster (21–39 ms vs 71–131 ms) | 2.9–4.2x faster (22–61 ms vs 90–234 ms) |
| edit and rebuild | 12–17x faster (4–6 ms vs 63–75 ms) | 4.8–7.0x faster (11–22 ms vs 68–114 ms) |
| binary | 13–24x smaller | 93–550x smaller (8–48 KiB vs 4.4 MiB) |

[SUPPORTED.md](SUPPORTED.md) breaks this down by area as a checklist.

## Requirements

- Linux x86-64
- A Rust toolchain that supports edition 2024 (rustup stable is fine)
- The C compiler driver `cc` (used to build the link line)
- A linker: wild, mold, ld.lld or ld. zustc picks the first one on PATH in the order wild > mold > ld.lld > ld.
- For zust-analyzer to resolve std definitions, rust-src: `rustup component add rust-src`

## Install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/mizchi/zust.git
```

```bash
cd zust
```

```bash
cargo install --path .
```

```bash
cargo install --path crates/analyzer
```

This puts `zustc` and `zust-analyzer` in `~/.cargo/bin`. You can also run `cargo build --release --workspace` and use
the binaries in `target/release/` without installing.

## Using zustc

### A single-file program

```bash
zustc hello.rs -o hello
```

```bash
./hello
```

- **Output path:** without `-o`, the output goes next to the input with the extension removed (`hello`).
- **Files next to the output:**
  - `hello.crcache2`: the cache
  - `hello.o`: the object file
  - `hello.link`: the saved link line
- **Rebuilds:** only the functions that changed are recompiled. If nothing changed, zustc does not even link.

`mod x;` reads `x.rs` or `x/mod.rs`.

### Check only

```bash
zustc check hello.rs
```

This runs up to type checking (no code generation) and prints all diagnostics. It also checks unreachable functions
and every requested instance of generic functions.

### Multiple crates

Pass a file that lists one crate per line. Each line is `lib|bin <name> <root file> [dependencies..]`, with paths
relative to that file:

```text
lib util util/src/lib.rs
lib geom geom/src/lib.rs util
bin app app/src/main.rs geom util
```

```bash
zustc build workspace.txt -o target
```

- Each crate gets its own object file and cache, and they are linked at the end.
- Changing the body of a function in a crate that others depend on does not recompile the dependents; zustc only
  relinks.
- See `tests/workspace/` for an example.
- Cargo.toml is not read.

### Options

| option | meaning |
|---|---|
| `-o PATH` | output path (the output directory for `build`) |
| `-O` | optimize: inline small functions and use Cranelift's `speed` level. Disables overflow checks |
| `--backend=cranelift\|minclif` | code generator (default cranelift; also `ZUSTC_BACKEND`) |
| `--linker=wild\|mold\|lld\|bfd\|PATH` | choose the linker |
| `--features=a,b` | enable `#[cfg(feature = "..")]` |
| `-j N` | number of code generation threads |
| `--time` | print the time of each phase and the peak RSS |
| `--no-cache` | neither read nor write the cache |

Panics are reported in the same form as rustc: `thread 'main' panicked at src/main.rs:LINE:COL:`, then the message,
then exit code 101. Integer overflow is checked as in a rustc debug build; `-O` turns the checks off.

## Using zust-analyzer

zust-analyzer is an LSP server over stdio; start `zust-analyzer` from your editor's LSP client. It treats the
directory with Cargo.toml as the workspace root and indexes:

- the crates: lib, bin, tests, examples and build.rs, plus the files reachable through `mod`
- std, from rust-src
- the dependencies listed in Cargo.toml, using the versions from Cargo.lock, that are present under
  `~/.cargo/registry/src`

### Neovim (0.11 or later)

```lua
vim.lsp.config('zust_analyzer', {
  cmd = { 'zust-analyzer' },
  filetypes = { 'rust' },
  root_markers = { 'Cargo.toml', '.git' },
})
vim.lsp.enable('zust_analyzer')
```

### Helix (`languages.toml`)

```toml
[language-server.zust-analyzer]
command = "zust-analyzer"

[[language]]
name = "rust"
language-servers = ["zust-analyzer"]
```

Any other editor works too, as long as its client can start an arbitrary command as an LSP server.

### Features

| feature | supported |
|---|---|
| documentSymbol / workspace/symbol | yes |

Rust のサブセットを速くインクリメンタルにビルドするコンパイラ **zustc** と、軽い LSP サーバ **zust-analyzer**。

- **zustc**: 自前のフロントエンド (lexer / parser / 型推論) と Cranelift (既定) か自前の x86-64 バックエンド minclif で
  コード生成する。開発中の「1 か所直してビルド」を速く、小さくすることに特化している。
  - 再ビルドの時間
  - ピークメモリ
  - キャッシュのディスク消費
  - 出力バイナリのサイズ

- **zust-analyzer**: エディタ向けの LSP サーバ。定義・参照・hover・補完・rename などを、字句の列と定義の表からの軽い解析で
  返す。普通の Rust のワークスペース (std と依存クレートも索引する) で使える。

> **状態**: 実験的なプロジェクト。zustc は Linux x86-64 だけで、Rust の全部は扱えない ([対応している言語](docs/ja/language.md))。
> 検査 (型、region の誤りを除く借用検査) は一部だけなので、rustc の代わりに正しさを確かめる道具ではない。zust-analyzer は rust-analyzer の一部の機能だけ。

どの変更も、これらが悪くならないときだけ残す。全体の計測で LSP の時間が上がったときは、同じマシンで 2 つのビルドを
交互に走らせて比べ直してから、揺れかどうかを決める。e598fdf の行はそうして比べた値で、起動の時間は 2 つの対象のファイルの合計。ほかの行は `bench/ci_bench.py` の全体の計測。

main に入るたびに測った数字の推移は [ベンチマークのダッシュボード](https://mizchi.github.io/zust/dev/bench/) にある
(GitHub Actions の共有のランナーで測るので、時間は揺れる。命令数の系列の方が差を見やすい)。

### rustc のテスト集をどれだけ通るか

rustc 自身の UI テスト (rust-lang/rust 1.100.0 の `tests/ui`、`python3 bench/rust_ui.py`) を zustc で走らせた結果。
zustc に求められるもの (nightly の機能・補助のクレート・特別なフラグが要らないもの) だけを数える:

| 種類 | 対象 | 通った |
|---|---:|---:|
| run-pass (ビルドでき、実行して同じ出力) | 2413 | 1536 (63.7%) |
| check-pass (`zustc check` が通す) | 1807 | 1271 (70.3%) |
| build-pass | 135 | 89 (65.9%) |
| compile-fail (注釈の行で拒む) | 7358 | 2844 (38.7%) |

分野ごとの内訳はチェックリストの形で [SUPPORTED.ja.md](SUPPORTED.ja.md) にある。

## 必要なもの

- Linux x86-64
- Rust のツールチェイン (edition 2024 が使えるもの。rustup の stable で可)
- C コンパイラのドライバ `cc` (リンク行を作るのに使う) と、リンカ
  - リンカは wild / mold / ld.lld / ld のどれか。PATH にある順に wild > mold > ld.lld > ld で選ぶ。
- zust-analyzer で std の定義を引くには rust-src: `rustup component add rust-src`

## インストール

```bash
git clone https://github.com/mizchi/zust.git
```

```bash
cd zust
```

```bash
cargo install --path .
```

```bash
cargo install --path crates/analyzer
```

`zustc` と `zust-analyzer` が `~/.cargo/bin` に入る。インストールせずに `cargo build --release --workspace` で
`target/release/` に作ってもよい。

## zustc の使い方

### 1 ファイルのプログラム

```bash
zustc hello.rs -o hello
```

```bash
./hello
```

`-o` を省くと、入力と同じ場所に拡張子なしの名前 (`hello`) で出す。出力の横にキャッシュ (`hello.crcache2`)、オブジェクト
(`hello.o`)、リンク行 (`hello.link`) を置く。2 回目からは変わった関数だけをコンパイルし直す。何も変わっていなければ
リンクもしない。

`mod x;` は `x.rs` / `x/mod.rs` を読む。

### 検査だけ

```bash
zustc check hello.rs
```

コード生成の手前 (型の検査) までして、すべての診断を出す。到達しない関数や、総称関数の要求されたインスタンスも検査する。

### 複数クレート

クレートを 1 行に 1 つ書いたファイルを渡す。書き方は `lib|bin <名前> <根のファイル> [依存するクレート..]` で、パスはこのファイルからの相対:

```text
lib util util/src/lib.rs
lib geom geom/src/lib.rs util
bin app app/src/main.rs geom util
```

```bash
zustc build workspace.txt -o target
```

クレートごとにオブジェクトとキャッシュを作ってリンクする。依存されるクレートの関数の本体を変えても、使う側はコンパイルし直さない
(リンクだけ)。例は `tests/workspace/`。Cargo.toml は読まない。

### オプション

| オプション | 意味 |
|---|---|
| `-o PATH` | 出力のパス (`build` では出力のディレクトリ) |
| `-O` | 最適化する: 小さい関数のインライン展開と Cranelift の `speed`。オーバーフローの検査をしない |
| `--backend=cranelift\|minclif` | コード生成 (既定 cranelift。環境変数 `ZUSTC_BACKEND` でも) |
| `--linker=wild\|mold\|lld\|bfd\|PATH` | リンカを選ぶ |
| `--features=a,b` | `#[cfg(feature = "..")]` を有効にする |
| `-j N` | コード生成のスレッド数 |
| `--time` | 段ごとの時間とピーク RSS を出す |
| `--no-cache` | キャッシュを読まず、書かない |

panic は rustc と同じ形 (`thread 'main' panicked at src/main.rs:行:列:` とメッセージ、終了コード 101) で出る。
オーバーフローは rustc の debug ビルドと同じく検査する (`-O` では検査しない)。

## zust-analyzer の使い方

stdio で話す LSP サーバ。エディタの LSP クライアントから `zust-analyzer` を起動する。Cargo.toml のあるディレクトリを
ワークスペースの根として、クレート (lib / bin / tests / examples / build.rs と `mod` で辿れるファイル)、std
(rust-src)、Cargo.toml に書いた依存クレート (版は Cargo.lock から。`~/.cargo/registry/src` にあるもの) を索引する。

### Neovim (0.11 以降)

```lua
vim.lsp.config('zust_analyzer', {
  cmd = { 'zust-analyzer' },
  filetypes = { 'rust' },
  root_markers = { 'Cargo.toml', '.git' },
})
vim.lsp.enable('zust_analyzer')
```

### Helix (`languages.toml`)

```toml
[language-server.zust-analyzer]
command = "zust-analyzer"

[[language]]
name = "rust"
language-servers = ["zust-analyzer"]
```

他のエディタでも、任意のコマンドを LSP サーバとして起動できるクライアントなら使える。

### 対応している機能

| 機能 | 対応 |
|---|---|
| documentSymbol / workspace/symbol | ○ |
| definition / references / documentHighlight | ○ |
| hover / completion / signatureHelp | ○ |
| rename / prepareRename | ○ (ワークスペースの中だけ書き換える) |
| publishDiagnostics | ○ (zustc の check の診断。zustc が扱えない書き方には誤った診断が出ることがある) |
| semanticTokens / inlayHint / codeAction / formatting | × |

ファイルの同期は全文 (didChange で本文全体を受け取る)。

### 設定 (環境変数)

| 変数 | 意味 |
|---|---|
| `ZUST_ANALYZER_MEM_MB` | ワークスペースのファイルの本文をメモリに持つ上限 (MB、既定 4)。超えた分は必要なときに読み直す |
| `ZUST_ANALYZER_NO_STD` | std の索引を作らない |
| `ZUST_ANALYZER_NO_DEPS` | 依存クレートの索引を作らない |
| `ZUST_ANALYZER_SYSROOT` | std のソースを探す sysroot (既定は `rustc --print sysroot`) |

rust-analyzer との違いで分かっているものは [TODO.md](TODO.md) にある。

- [docs/ja/language.md](docs/ja/language.md): zustc が扱える Rust のサブセットと、扱えないもの
- [docs/ja/architecture.md](docs/ja/architecture.md): crate の構成、処理の流れ、インクリメンタルビルドのしくみ、値の表現

- [TODO.md](TODO.md): これからやること (英語)

Rust 本体と同じく、次のどちらかを選んで使える (デュアルライセンス)。

- Apache License, Version 2.0 ([LICENSE-APACHE](LICENSE-APACHE))

提供されたものとする。

`cratebench/vendor/` の中のクレート (ベンチマーク用の git submodule) は、それぞれの上流のライセンスに従う。

# Contributing

English | [日本語](CONTRIBUTING.ja.md)

This document covers how to change and extend zust (zustc and zust-analyzer). See [README.md](README.md) for usage
and [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) for how it works inside.

## Setup

In addition to the requirements in the README, the following tools are used:

- rustc: `tests/compare.sh` and `tests/probe.sh` build the same programs with rustc and compare the results.
- python3: the benchmark scripts (`bench/*.py`).
- valgrind (optional): `tests/compare.sh` also checks for memory errors and leaks.
- rust-analyzer (optional): `bench/lsp_parity.py` and `bench/ide_golden_ra.py` compare answers against it.
- cargo-mutants (optional): mutation testing.
- wild (optional): faster linking. The benchmark numbers are measured with wild.
- Node 24+ and a TypeSafe API key (optional): checking that English and Japanese documents agree (jev-lint).

```bash
cargo build --release --workspace
```

This builds `target/release/zustc` and `target/release/zust-analyzer`. Most tests and scripts use these two release
builds.

`cratebench/run.py` and `bench/deps_bench.py` use the sources of real crates from git submodules. Fetch them once
(or clone with `git clone --recurse-submodules`):

```bash
git submodule update --init cratebench/vendor
```

## Repository layout

| path | contents |
|---|---|
| `src/` | the `zustc` CLI (`src/main.rs`) and re-exports of the crates below |
| `crates/base` → `syntax` → `sema` → `typeck` → `codegen` → `core` | the compiler layers (each depends on the ones before it) |
| `crates/minclif` / `crates/clif` / `crates/ir` | our own x86-64 backend / the Cranelift backend / the instruction-stream types |
| `crates/ide` | editor analysis (symbols, definition, references, hover, completion). Not used by the compiler |
| `crates/analyzer` | the LSP server `zust-analyzer` |
| `examples/` | inputs compiled by zustc (not Cargo examples) |
| `tests/` | zustc tests (comparisons with rustc, caching, self-hosting, and more) |
| `benches/` / `bench/` | criterion benchmarks / benchmark and regression-monitoring scripts |
| `cratebench/` | a benchmark that builds small real-world crates |
| `docs/` | the language subset, the design, and work reports (English; Japanese versions in `docs/ja/`) |

What each crate contains is described in detail in [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md).

## Tests

```bash
cargo test --release --workspace
```

This runs all the tests:

- unit tests (the lexer and others)
- diagnostics from check: it keeps going after an error, and it reports errors in generic function bodies even
  through cached callers
- caching and incremental builds
- panic locations and multiple crates
- the size budget (`tests/budget.rs`)
- zust-ide golden files
- zust-analyzer integration tests (they drive the real binary over stdio)

If you only changed the LSP side, this is enough:

```bash
cargo test --release -p zust-ide -p zust-analyzer
```

### Comparing results with rustc

```bash
tests/compare.sh
```

Builds `examples/*.rs` with both zustc and rustc and checks that the output and exit code match. It compares both a
build without a cache and a rebuild from the cache. If valgrind is available, memory errors and definite leaks also
fail the run.

```bash
tests/probe.sh
```

Compares small programs that use common features (`tests/probe/*.rs`) with rustc and prints how many pass. When you
add a language feature, add a probe here.

### Self-hosting

```bash
tests/selfhost.sh
```

Compiles parts of zustc's own source (lexer, prelude, link, macros, parse, type inference, and more) with zustc and
checks that the output is the same as the rustc-compiled version.

```bash
tests/selfhost_compiler.sh
```

Compiles the whole compiler with both zustc and rustc and checks that the two resulting compilers produce the same
`.o` files. It also compiles the compiler again with the zustc-built version and checks that the result is the same
(a fixed point).

### rustc's own test suite

`bench/rust_ui.py` runs zustc against rustc's UI tests (rust-lang/rust `tests/ui`, pinned to the commit of rustc
1.100.0). Fetch them once (a sparse clone of only `tests/ui`, about 170 MB, into `out/rust-tests`):

```bash
python3 bench/rust_ui.py --fetch
```

```bash
python3 bench/rust_ui.py --baseline bench/rust_ui_passing.txt --check
```

Each test's kind comes from its header directives, as in compiletest. A run-pass test must build, exit 0 and print
its `.run.stdout`. A check-pass test must pass `zustc check`. A compile-fail test must be rejected with an error on a
line that one of its `//~ ERROR` annotations points at. Tests that need what zustc cannot be asked for (nightly
`#![feature]`, auxiliary crates, `compile-flags`, `revisions`, other targets) are counted as not applicable.

`bench/rust_ui_passing.txt` lists the tests zustc passes. CI fails if one of them no longer passes. When a change
makes more tests pass, rewrite the list:

```bash
python3 bench/rust_ui.py --baseline bench/rust_ui_passing.txt --write-baseline
```

`--filter SUBSTR` runs only matching paths, `--kinds run-pass` one kind, and `out/rust_ui_results.txt` has the result
of every test.

### Golden files

`crates/ide/tests/golden/*.txt` record zust-ide's answers. When you change answers on purpose, rewrite them with:

```bash
UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 cargo test -p zust-ide --test golden
```

Before rewriting, make sure the diff is an improvement. To see whether the answers now agree with rust-analyzer, run:

```bash
python3 bench/ide_golden_ra.py --detail
```

## Benchmarks and regression monitoring

```bash
bench/regress.sh save
```

Before adding a feature, save the current state as the baseline `main`.

```bash
bench/regress.sh
```

Compares against the baseline. It fails if any of these happen:

- criterion (`benches/compile.rs`) reports a regression
- the size budget (`bench/budget.txt`) is exceeded
- output differs from rustc (`tests/compare.sh`)

### Rules for judging

- Changes below 5% are ignored. The significance level is 1%. The cold benchmarks vary by ±10%, so their threshold
  is 15%.
- Values depend on the state of the machine. To compare, measure at the same time as the baseline commit (benchmarking
  HEAD in a git worktree at the same time is reliable). To track down a cause, callgrind instruction counts are stable.
- The size budget holds an upper limit in bytes for each example's binary, `.o` and cache.
  - To increase it on purpose, use `UPDATE_BUDGET=1`.
  - If you only added new examples, use `UPDATE_BUDGET=new` (existing limits stay unchanged).

  Before loosening the budget, find out why the size grew (for example, more prelude items attached). Past cases are
  in [docs/reports/2026-11-15-17-regression-catches.md](docs/reports/2026-11-15-17-regression-catches.md).

### Other benchmarks

| script | what it measures |
|---|---|
| `python3 bench/vs_rustc.py [NAME..]` | comparison with rustc (cold, no-op and one-edit build times, disk, binary size, run time) |
| `python3 bench/runtime.py` | run time and binary size only (a lighter version) |
| `python3 bench/run.py 1000 5000` | cold / no-op / one-function edit on generated programs with N functions |
| `python3 bench/ws_bench.py --rustc` | a multi-crate workspace |
| `python3 bench/deps_bench.py` | multiple crates with many dependencies |
| `python3 bench/lsp_compare.py --cold` | LSP server speed (against rust-analyzer / rust-glancer) |
| `python3 bench/lsp_parity.py` | compares LSP answers with rust-analyzer |

`lsp_parity.py` can compare against the previous numbers and show the difference:

```bash
python3 bench/lsp_parity.py --compare bench/lsp_parity.json --json bench/lsp_parity.json --out bench/lsp_parity_result.md
```

Add `--detail` to print the places where the answers differ.

### Mutation testing

```bash
bench/mutants.sh diff
```

Mutates only the lines changed since origin/main and checks whether the tests catch the mutants. You can also narrow
it with `bench/mutants.sh pkg zust-ide` (a crate) or `bench/mutants.sh file crates/ide/src/symbols.rs` (a file).
Mutants the tests miss are written to `mutants.out/missed.txt`; add tests to kill them.

## CI and the benchmark dashboard

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs a release build, `cargo test --release --workspace`, `tests/compare.sh` and the
  tests/ui baseline check on every push and pull request. The size budget depends on the linker, so CI installs wild 0.11.0 and measures with
  `ZUSTC_BENCH_LINKER=wild` (`bench/budget.txt` also holds wild sizes).
- `.github/workflows/bench.yml` runs `bench/ci_bench.py` on every push to main and stores the results in `dev/bench/`
  on the gh-pages branch with
  [github-action-benchmark](https://github.com/benchmark-action/github-action-benchmark). The dashboard is at
  https://mizchi.github.io/zust/dev/bench/ (publish the gh-pages branch in the repository's Settings → Pages).
  It tracks:
  - zustc: build (cold / no-op / one-function edit) and check times and instruction counts for programs with 1000 and
    5000 functions, peak RSS, output and cache size, and run time of `bench/rt`
  - zust-analyzer: p50 of each query in `bench/lsp_parity.py` (on zustc's own sources), time from startup until
    indexed, and RSS
  - the share of answers that agree with rust-analyzer
  - the pass rates on rustc's tests/ui
  - Anything that got worse by 30% or more since the previous run (5% for the agreement ratios) produces a warning in
    the workflow result. It does not fail the run.

To measure the same things locally:

```bash
python3 bench/ci_bench.py --out-dir out/ci
```

## English and Japanese documents

Each English document has a Japanese translation: `README.md` / `README.ja.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` /
`CONTRIBUTING.ja.md`, and `docs/X.md` / `docs/ja/X.md` (reports included). When you change one, change the other
too. [jev-lint](https://github.com/mizchi/jev-lint) `docs` asks a model whether each pair still says the same thing.

- `scripts/docs_manifest.py` writes the jev-lint manifests (`.jev-lint/documents*.json`) from the pairs;
  `--check` fails if a file has no counterpart or a manifest is out of date.
- `scripts/docs_check.sh` replays the recorded verdicts (`.jev-lint/*-baseline.json`) against the current documents.
  It is offline and needs no API key; CI runs it. It fails if a pair contradicts, or if a document changed after its
  verdict was recorded.
- `scripts/docs_check.sh --update` asks the model again for the manifests whose documents changed and rewrites the
  records. It needs `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` (or `TYPESAFEAI_API_KEY`) from https://typesafe.ai; the document text is
  sent to that API. A full run of all 64 pairs costs about $0.03.

Enable the pre-commit hook once per clone:

```bash
git config core.hooksPath .githooks
```

When a commit touches Markdown, the hook runs `scripts/docs_check.sh --update`, adds the updated records to the
commit, and stops the commit if a pair contradicts. A verdict is a model's judgment: read the reported pair and fix
whichever side is wrong (or, if the finding is wrong, commit with `--no-verify`).

## Debugging environment variables

| variable | meaning |
|---|---|
| `ZUSTC_IR_VERIFY=1` | check that the value types of the rebuilt instructions match the type checker's record |
| `ZUSTC_CLIF_VERIFY=1` / `ZUSTC_CLIF_DUMP=1` | verify / dump the Cranelift IR |
| `ZUSTC_PREP_VERIFY=1` | compare the result of incremental preprocessing with a full rerun |
| `ZUSTC_DUMP_PRE=FILE` | write the source after preprocessing (`macro_rules!` expansion, merging `mod x;` files) to FILE |
| `ZUSTC_LOG_COMPILED=1` | print the names of compiled functions (and why, for those that could not be read from the cache) |
| `ZUSTC_PROF=1` | print detailed time per phase |
| `ZUSTC_NO_STRIP=1` | keep symbols in the output (to see function names in callgrind and similar tools) |
| `ZUSTC_BENCH_LINKER` | pin the linker used by the criterion benchmarks |

The other `ZUSTC_NO_*` variables turn off one optimization or incremental mechanism at a time, for comparison. Search
the code for the name to see what each one does.

## How to make changes

- When adding a language feature, first add a program to `examples/` or `tests/probe/` that compares with rustc.
- After a change, pass `cargo test --release --workspace`. If you changed the compiler, also pass `tests/compare.sh`.
  If the change affects speed or size, also pass `bench/regress.sh`.
- If you changed LSP answers, check with `bench/lsp_parity.py` that agreement and times did not get worse.
- After a substantial piece of work, write a report (next section).
- Record differences from rust-analyzer and anything left undone in [TODO.md](TODO.md).

### Writing reports

Work reports go in `docs/reports/YYYY-MM-DD-NN-<slug>.md`, in English. If you also write a Japanese version, put it
in `docs/ja/reports/` under the same name.

- `YYYY-MM-DD` is the day of the work.
- `NN` is the order within that day (starting at 01).
- `<slug>` is a short kebab-case description.

Sorting by file name gives date order. Use this form:

```markdown
# Title

Date: YYYY-MM-DD

What was done, why, how it was measured, the results (numbers), what was learned, what is left
```

Keep the numbers as they were when measured (do not rewrite them later). After writing a report, add a line to the
list in [docs/reports/README.md](docs/reports/README.md) (and to
[docs/ja/reports/README.md](docs/ja/reports/README.md) if you wrote a Japanese version).

### Commits

- Keep one coherent change per commit.
- In the message, name the area (`ide:` / `analyzer:` / `docs:` and so on) and say what changed.

# 開発のしかた

[English](CONTRIBUTING.md) | 日本語

zust (zustc と zust-analyzer) を直す・足すときの手順。使い方は [README.ja.md](README.ja.md)、中のしくみは
[docs/ja/architecture.md](docs/ja/architecture.md)。

## 準備

README の「必要なもの」に加えて、次のものを使う。

- rustc: tests/compare.sh や tests/probe.sh が、同じプログラムを rustc でもビルドして結果を比べる。
- python3: ベンチマークのスクリプト (`bench/*.py`)。
- valgrind (あれば): tests/compare.sh がメモリエラーとリークも見る。
- rust-analyzer (あれば): `bench/lsp_parity.py` と `bench/ide_golden_ra.py` が答えを比べる。
- cargo-mutants (あれば): ミューテーションテスト。
- wild (あれば): リンクが速くなる。ベンチマークの数字は wild で測っている。
- Node 24 以上と TypeSafe の API キー (あれば): 英語と日本語の文書が食い違っていないかの確認 (jev-lint)。

```bash
cargo build --release --workspace
```

`cratebench/run.py` と `bench/deps_bench.py` は、実在のクレートのソースを git submodule から使う。最初に一度取ってくる
(`git clone --recurse-submodules` で clone してもよい)。

```bash
git submodule update --init cratebench/vendor
```

`target/release/zustc` と `target/release/zust-analyzer` ができる。テストやスクリプトの多くは、この 2 つの release
ビルドを使う。

## リポジトリの構成

| 場所 | 中身 |
|---|---|
| `src/` | `zustc` の CLI (`src/main.rs`) と、下の crate の再輸出 |
| `crates/base` → `syntax` → `sema` → `typeck` → `codegen` → `core` | コンパイラの層 (下から順に依存する) |
| `crates/minclif` / `crates/clif` / `crates/ir` | 自前の x86-64 バックエンド / Cranelift のバックエンド / 命令の列の型 |
| `crates/ide` | エディタ向けの解析 (シンボル・定義・参照・hover・補完)。コンパイラ本体からは使わない |
| `crates/analyzer` | LSP サーバ `zust-analyzer` |
| `examples/` | zustc でコンパイルする入力 (Cargo の example ではない) |
| `tests/` | zustc のテスト (rustc と比べるもの、キャッシュ、セルフホストなど) |
| `benches/` / `bench/` | criterion のベンチ / ベンチマークと回帰監視のスクリプト |
| `cratebench/` | 実在の小さなクレートをビルドするベンチ |
| `docs/` | 言語のサブセット、設計、作業のレポート (英語。日本語版は `docs/ja/`) |

crate ごとの詳しい中身は [docs/ja/architecture.md](docs/ja/architecture.md) にある。

## テスト

```bash
cargo test --release --workspace
```

全部のテスト。次のものが入っている。

- lexer などの単体テスト
- check の診断 (エラーの後も止まらないこと、キャッシュされた呼び出し元越しに総称関数の本体のエラーを拾うこと)
- キャッシュとインクリメンタルビルド
- panic の場所、複数クレート
- サイズ予算 (`tests/budget.rs`)
- zust-ide のゴールデン
- zust-analyzer の結合テスト (実際のバイナリを stdio で動かす)

LSP の側だけを直したときは、次のコマンドで足りる。

```bash
cargo test --release -p zust-ide -p zust-analyzer
```

### rustc と結果を比べる

```bash
tests/compare.sh
```

`examples/*.rs` を zustc と rustc の両方でビルドし、出力と終了コードが一致するかを確かめる。キャッシュなしのビルドと、
キャッシュからの再ビルドの両方を比べる。valgrind があれば、メモリエラーと確実なリークも失敗にする。

```bash
tests/probe.sh
```

よく使う機能の小さいプログラム (`tests/probe/*.rs`) を rustc と比べ、通った数を出す。言語の機能を足したら、ここに
probe を足す。

### セルフホスト

```bash
tests/selfhost.sh
```

zustc 自身のソースの一部 (lexer / prelude / link / macros / parse / 型推論 など) を zustc でコンパイルし、rustc で
コンパイルしたものと出力が同じかを確かめる。

```bash
tests/selfhost_compiler.sh
```

コンパイラ全体を zustc と rustc の両方でコンパイルする。できた 2 つのコンパイラが同じ `.o` を出すかを確かめる。zustc 版で
自分自身をもう一度コンパイルし、同じものになるか (不動点) も見る。

### rustc 自身のテスト集

`bench/rust_ui.py` は、rustc の UI テスト (rust-lang/rust の `tests/ui`。rustc 1.100.0 のコミットに固定) を zustc で
走らせる。最初に一度取ってくる (`tests/ui` だけの部分 clone、約 170 MB を `out/rust-tests` に):

```bash
python3 bench/rust_ui.py --fetch
```

```bash
python3 bench/rust_ui.py --baseline bench/rust_ui_passing.txt --check
```

テストの種類は、compiletest と同じく頭の指示から決める。run-pass のテストは、ビルドでき、終了コード 0 で、
`.run.stdout` と同じものを出すこと。check-pass のテストは `zustc check` が通すこと。compile-fail のテストは、
`//~ ERROR` の注釈が指す行にエラーを出して拒むこと。zustc に求められないもの (nightly の `#![feature]`・補助の
クレート・`compile-flags`・`revisions`・ほかのターゲット) が要るテストは「対象外」に数える。

`bench/rust_ui_passing.txt` は zustc が通るテストの一覧。そのどれかが通らなくなると CI が失敗する。変更で通る
テストが増えたら、一覧を書き直す:

```bash
python3 bench/rust_ui.py --baseline bench/rust_ui_passing.txt --write-baseline
```

`--filter 文字列` でパスが合うものだけ、`--kinds run-pass` で 1 つの種類だけを走らせる。すべてのテストの結果は
`out/rust_ui_results.txt` にある。

### ゴールデン

`crates/ide/tests/golden/*.txt` は zust-ide の答えの記録。意図して答えを変えたら、次のコマンドで書き直す。

```bash
UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 cargo test -p zust-ide --test golden
```

書き直す前に、差分が改善かどうかを確かめる。rust-analyzer と同じ答えになったかは、次のコマンドで見られる。

```bash
python3 bench/ide_golden_ra.py --detail
```

## ベンチマークと回帰監視

```bash
bench/regress.sh save
```

機能を足す前に、今の状態をベースライン `main` として保存する。

```bash
bench/regress.sh
```

ベースラインと比べる。次のどれかがあれば失敗する。

- criterion (`benches/compile.rs`) が「回帰」と判定したもの
- サイズ予算 (`bench/budget.txt`) の超過
- rustc との出力の差 (`tests/compare.sh`)

### 判定の決まり

- 5% 未満の変化は無視する。有意水準は 1%。cold 系は ±10% ぶれるので、閾値を 15% にしている。
- 値はマシンの状態で変わる。比べるときは同じ時間帯に、ベースラインのコミットと並べて測る (git worktree で HEAD を同時に
  ベンチすると確か)。原因を詰めるには callgrind の命令数が安定している。
- サイズ予算は、例ごとに、バイナリ・`.o`・キャッシュの上限のバイト数を持つ。
  - 意図して増やすなら `UPDATE_BUDGET=1`。
  - 新しい例を足しただけなら `UPDATE_BUDGET=new` (既存の上限は変えない)。

  予算を緩める前に、増えた理由 (付く prelude が増えた、など) を詰める。これまでの例は
  [docs/ja/reports/2026-11-15-17-regression-catches.md](docs/ja/reports/2026-11-15-17-regression-catches.md) にある。

### ほかのベンチマーク

| スクリプト | 何を測るか |
|---|---|
| `python3 bench/vs_rustc.py [NAME..]` | rustc との比較 (cold・no-op・1 か所編集の時間、ディスク、バイナリ、実行時間) |
| `python3 bench/runtime.py` | 実行時間とバイナリだけ (軽い版) |
| `python3 bench/run.py 1000 5000` | N 関数の生成したプログラムでの cold / no-op / 1 関数編集 |
| `python3 bench/ws_bench.py --rustc` | 複数クレートのワークスペース |
| `python3 bench/deps_bench.py` | 依存の多い複数クレート |
| `python3 bench/lsp_compare.py --cold` | LSP サーバの速さ (rust-analyzer / rust-glancer と) |
| `python3 bench/lsp_parity.py` | LSP の答えを rust-analyzer と比べる |

`lsp_parity.py` は、前回の数字と比べて差を出せる。

```bash
python3 bench/lsp_parity.py --compare bench/lsp_parity.json --json bench/lsp_parity.json --out bench/lsp_parity_result.md
```

`--detail` を付けると、違った所を出す。

### ミューテーションテスト

```bash
bench/mutants.sh diff
```

origin/main からの差分の行だけを変異させ、テストで見つかるかを見る。`bench/mutants.sh pkg zust-ide` (クレート) や
`bench/mutants.sh file crates/ide/src/symbols.rs` (ファイル) でも絞れる。見つからなかった変異は
`mutants.out/missed.txt` に出る。テストを足して潰す。

## CI とベンチマークのダッシュボード

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: push と pull request ごとに、release ビルド、`cargo test --release --workspace`、
  `tests/compare.sh`、tests/ui の一覧との比較を走らせる。サイズ予算はリンカで変わるので、CI は wild 0.11.0 を入れて `ZUSTC_BENCH_LINKER=wild` で測る
  (`bench/budget.txt` も wild の大きさ)。
- `.github/workflows/bench.yml`: main への push ごとに `bench/ci_bench.py` を走らせ、
  [github-action-benchmark](https://github.com/benchmark-action/github-action-benchmark) で gh-pages ブランチの `dev/bench/` に
  結果を積む。ダッシュボードは https://mizchi.github.io/zust/dev/bench/ (リポジトリの Settings → Pages で gh-pages ブランチを
  公開しておく)。
  - zustc: 1000 / 5000 関数のプログラムのビルド (cold / no-op / 1 関数編集)・check の時間と命令数、ピーク RSS、出力と
    キャッシュの大きさ、`bench/rt` の実行時間
  - zust-analyzer: `bench/lsp_parity.py` (zustc 自身のソース) の各問い合わせの p50、起動から索引ができるまで、RSS
  - rust-analyzer と同じ答えを返した割合
  - rustc の tests/ui の通った割合
  - 前回より 30% 以上悪くなった (一致の割合は 5%) ものは、ワークフローの結果に警告が出る (失敗にはしない)

ローカルで同じものを測るには:

```bash
python3 bench/ci_bench.py --out-dir out/ci
```

## 英語の文書と日本語訳

英語の文書にはそれぞれ日本語訳がある: `README.md` / `README.ja.md`、`CONTRIBUTING.md` / `CONTRIBUTING.ja.md`、
`docs/X.md` / `docs/ja/X.md` (レポートも)。片方を変えたら、もう片方も変える。
[jev-lint](https://github.com/mizchi/jev-lint) の `docs` が、それぞれの組が同じことを言っているかをモデルに聞く。

- `scripts/docs_manifest.py` は、組から jev-lint のマニフェスト (`.jev-lint/documents*.json`) を書く。`--check` は、
  相手のないファイルがあるか、マニフェストが古ければ失敗する。
- `scripts/docs_check.sh` は、記録した判定 (`.jev-lint/*-baseline.json`) を今の文書で読み直す。オフラインで、API キーは
  要らない (CI が走らせる)。組が食い違っているか、判定を記録した後に文書が変わっていれば失敗する。
- `scripts/docs_check.sh --update` は、文書が変わったマニフェストだけをモデルに判定させ直し、記録を書き直す。
  https://typesafe.ai の `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` (か `TYPESAFEAI_API_KEY`) が要る。文書の本文はその API に送られる。64 組を
  全部判定して約 $0.03。

コミットフックは、clone ごとに一度有効にする。

```bash
git config core.hooksPath .githooks
```

Markdown を変えたコミットでは、フックが `scripts/docs_check.sh --update` を走らせ、書き直した記録をコミットに足し、組が
食い違っていればコミットを止める。判定はモデルの判断なので、出た組を読んで間違っている側を直す (判定の方が間違っていれば
`--no-verify` でコミットする)。

## デバッグ用の環境変数

| 変数 | 意味 |
|---|---|
| `ZUSTC_IR_VERIFY=1` | 組み立て直した命令の値の型が、型検査の記録と同じかを確かめる |
| `ZUSTC_CLIF_VERIFY=1` / `ZUSTC_CLIF_DUMP=1` | Cranelift の IR を検証する / 出す |
| `ZUSTC_PREP_VERIFY=1` | 前処理の差分の結果を、全部やり直した結果と比べる |
| `ZUSTC_DUMP_PRE=FILE` | 前処理 (macro_rules! の展開・`mod x;` の結合) の後のソースを FILE に書く |
| `ZUSTC_LOG_COMPILED=1` | コンパイルした関数の名前を出す (キャッシュから読めなかったものはその理由も) |
| `ZUSTC_PROF=1` | 段ごとの時間を細かく出す |
| `ZUSTC_NO_STRIP=1` | 出力のシンボルを残す (callgrind などで関数名を見る) |
| `ZUSTC_BENCH_LINKER` | criterion のベンチのリンカを固定する |

ほかの `ZUSTC_NO_*` は、最適化やインクリメンタルの仕掛けを 1 つずつ切って比べるためのもの。名前でコードを検索すると
意味が分かる。

## 変更の進め方

- 言語の機能を足すときは、まず `examples/` か `tests/probe/` に rustc と比べるプログラムを足す。
- 変更の後は `cargo test --release --workspace` を通す。コンパイラを変えたら `tests/compare.sh` も通す。
  速さやサイズに効く変更なら `bench/regress.sh` も通す。
- LSP の答えを変えたら、`bench/lsp_parity.py` で一致の割合と時間が下がっていないことを見る。
- まとまった作業をしたら、レポートを書く (次の節)。
- rust-analyzer との違いや、残したことは [TODO.md](TODO.md) に書く (英語)。

### レポートの書き方

作業の記録は `docs/reports/YYYY-MM-DD-NN-<slug>.md` に英語で置く。日本語版を書くなら、同じ名前で `docs/ja/reports/` に置く。

- `YYYY-MM-DD` は作業した日。
- `NN` はその日の中の順番 (01 から)。
- `<slug>` は内容を表す短い kebab-case。

ファイル名で並べると日付順になる。中身は次の形にする。

```markdown
# Title

Date: YYYY-MM-DD

What was done, why, how it was measured, the results (numbers), what was learned, what is left
```

数字は測った時点のものとして残す (後から書き換えない)。書いたら、[docs/reports/README.md](docs/reports/README.md) の
一覧に 1 行足す (日本語版を書いたら [docs/ja/reports/README.md](docs/ja/reports/README.md) にも)。

### コミット

- 1 つのコミットは 1 つのまとまった変更にする。
- メッセージは、どの部分か (`ide:` / `analyzer:` / `docs:` など) と、何を変えたかを書く。
- 名前は zustc / zust-analyzer / zust-* に揃える。

## ライセンス

送られた貢献は、明示しない限り、README の「ライセンス」のとおり MIT OR Apache-2.0 で提供されたものとする。他のプロジェクトの
コードを取り込むときは、ライセンスが合うものだけにし、上流のリポジトリを git submodule にする (`cratebench/vendor/` と同じ) か、元のライセンスのファイルも一緒に置く。

# What zustc supports

Status as of 2026-11-18, updated with each round of work. The percentages are rustc's own UI tests that pass in that area
(`python3 bench/rust_ui.py`, rust-lang/rust tests/ui at 1.100.0; run-pass + check-pass + build-pass of the directory).
[TODO.md](TODO.md) has the work list; the [reports](docs/reports/) explain each step.

- `[x]` works for ordinary code (most tests of the area pass)
- `[ ]` partial or missing; the note says what is left

## Overall

- [x] tests/ui run-pass: 63.7% (1536 / 2413)
- [x] tests/ui check-pass: 70.3% (1271 / 1807)
- [x] tests/ui build-pass: 65.9% (89 / 135)
- [ ] tests/ui compile-fail (an error on an annotated line): 38.7% (2844 / 7358)
- [x] real crates: fnv, adler2, hex, itoa, rustc-hash and cfg-if build and give the same output (6 / 6)
- [x] zust-analyzer answers like rust-analyzer: 95.4% (rust-analyzer: 96.2%)

## Language

- [x] numbers, arithmetic, overflow checks: 89.7%
- [x] `for` / `while` / `loop`, labels: 88.7%
- [x] enums, `#[repr(u8)]`, auto-sized tags: 82.8%
- [x] `cfg`: 81.2%
- [x] bindings, patterns, slice patterns, or-patterns (also with guards): 72–81%
- [x] `match`: 78.0%
- [x] name resolution: 77.1%
- [x] statics: ints, floats, raw pointers, fn pointers, `const fn` calls: 75.0%
- [x] structs, `..base` (field by field): 74.2%
- [x] type aliases and paths (`impl foo::Point`) as impl self types, discriminants from constants and earlier variants, where clauses on concrete types
- [x] syntax: GAT bindings, `dyn for<'a> Fn`, 2015 anonymous parameters, raw lifetimes `'r#a`, half-open range patterns, shebangs, Unicode white space; `macro_rules!` fragments matched by kind (`ident`, `literal`, `lifetime`, `vis`)
- [x] methods of `impl Tr for Box<S>` (a Box impl next to a blanket impl of the same trait is E0119), `..b` / `..=b` / `..` values, `wrapping_shl` / `checked_shl` / `overflowing_shl` / `reverse_bits`
- [x] let chains (`if let A = x && cond`), `&raw const` / `&raw mut`
- [x] parser: 73.7%
- [x] closures (capture, `Fn` traits, `move`): 71.7%
- [x] derives: `Debug`, `Clone`, `Copy`, `PartialEq`/`Eq`, `PartialOrd`/`Ord`, `Hash`, `Default`: 68.2%
- [x] imports, `use`: 67.0%
- [x] associated types: 63.6%
- [x] generics: 61.9% (an integer literal for `T: Foo` takes the one integer type that implements Foo; a type
  parameter known only from the expected type is not inferred)
- [ ] consts: 54.9% (no heap values, no generic `const fn`; a const of a generic impl (`const C: Option<T> = None`) takes its type at each use)
- [ ] drop: 53.6% (the drop order of some temporaries differs)
- [ ] traits: 51.0% (generic traits, blanket impls, `dyn` (also `dyn Tr<A>`), `impl .. for dyn Tr` work; no coherence)
- [ ] `macro_rules!`: 47.1% (hygiene for `let`, labels, arm bindings; not every fragment kind)
- [ ] unions: 46.2% (no `repr(packed)`)
- [ ] const generics: 43.6% (no `generic_const_exprs`)
- [ ] generic associated types: 40.0%
- [ ] casts (`as _` / `as *const _` take the source or expected type; a pointer of unknown kind is E0641): 34.5%
- [ ] `impl Trait`: 29.7% (return position, also in trait methods; not from generic fns, not nested, no TAIT)
- [ ] layout: `repr(packed)` / `repr(align)` are ignored: 12–33%

## Checks (compile-fail)

- [x] borrow checking: moves, conflicting loans, escapes, mutability: borrowck 49.4%
  ([report 08](docs/reports/2026-11-18-08-borrow-checking.md))
- [x] type errors, missing items, generics declarations (E0403, E0207, E0392, E0072 ..): typeck 53.4%, structs 66.7%

  union field reads (not yet inside closures or consts, and not the `unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn` lint)
- [ ] region errors against signatures (E0621, E0521): regions 12.9%, lifetimes 19.5%
- [ ] coherence, bounds of blanket impls, dyn compatibility (E0038), the bindings of `dyn Tr<A = T>` against the associated type's bounds (done when T is a primitive, `str` or a struct name)
- [ ] lints and warnings: lint 8.3%
- [ ] editions (2015-only errors)

## Runtime and std

- [x] the prelude (zustc's own small std): `Option`/`Result`, `Vec`, `String`, `HashMap`/`HashSet`,
  `BTreeMap`/`BTreeSet`, `VecDeque`, `BinaryHeap`, `Rc`/`Arc`, `Cell`/`RefCell`, `Mutex`, `OnceLock`, `ManuallyDrop`,
  `Duration`, `AtomicPtr`, `RangeTo` / `RangeFull` as types, `Fuse`, `iter::Empty`, `NonNull`, `Pin` (a plain pointer: `Pin::new`, `get_mut`, `into_inner`, deref), `UnsafeCell`, `PhantomData`, atomics, `mpsc`, `mem::*`, `ptr::{read, write, drop_in_place, null}`,

- [ ] run time: zustc is 1.2–3.6x slower than rustc `-O` on small programs (faster than rustc's debug build);

- [x] against relax (a Rust JIT), source to finished output: 5.3–12x faster cold, 1.3–3.4x on a no-op run, 1.6–18x

# Design

## Crate layout (Cargo workspace)

The layers go in this order: base → syntax → sema → typeck → codegen → core (driver). syntax, sema and typeck are the parts that the compiler, the LSP and analysis
share. The LSP uses core without the feature `build`, and does not depend on the backends (codegen / minclif / Cranelift).

| crate | Contents | Depends on |
|---|---|---|
| `crates/base` (`zust-base`) | fxhash (FxMap / FxSet), key (cache keys), prof (time per stage) | none |
| `crates/syntax` (`zust-syntax`) | front (the flow preprocessing → splitting into items (diff) → attaching the prelude, plus FrontMemo, the memory kept across edits) / lexer / parse (own syntax tree) / cfg / macros / ctors / prep (preprocessing diff) / srcmap / stub / types (item summary types), types_enc / enc (serialization) / ast_types / ast_closure / ast_summary (item summaries) / prelude (selection and prelude_lib.rs.in, build.rs) | base, proc-macro2 |
| `crates/sema` (`zust-sema`) | program (tables of names, types, traits and impls; instances) / solver / ast_infer (type inference) / ast_consteval | syntax |
| `crates/ir` (`zust-ir`) | Types for the instruction sequence (Type / Value / Block / Op …), and Recorder, which only records instructions (it remembers the types of values) | none |
| `crates/typeck` (`zust-typeck`) | acg (records the syntax tree as an instruction sequence; type checking errors come out here) / cache2 (Blob serialization) | sema, ir, proc-macro2 |
| `crates/codegen` (`zust-codegen`) | lower (rebuilds the record into minclif and turns it into machine code; for Cranelift it passes it to zust-clif) / link | typeck, minclif |
| `crates/core` (`zust-core`) | driver2 (Session2: analysis, check, cache), and, with the feature `build` (default), driver2/build.rs (machine code, fork parallelization, objects, linking, workspaces). Re-exports the lower layers | typeck, (with build) codegen |
| `crates/ide` (`zust-ide`) | Analysis for editors: symbols (symbols for documentSymbol / workspace/symbol) / navigate (definition, references, hover, completion; light type estimation from the token sequence and the definition table). Not used by the compiler itself | syntax |
| `crates/analyzer` (`zust-analyzer`) | LSP server (binary `zust-analyzer`). Diagnostics come from driver2's check; everything else from ide. Workspace file contents are kept up to a memory limit | core (without build), ide, serde_json |
| `crates/minclif` | A small x86-64 backend with a Cranelift-like API (register allocation, turning fields of stack structs into variables, ELF .o). `from_recording` rebuilds a record | ir |
| `crates/clif` (`zust-clif`) | The Cranelift backend of driver2: turns the instruction sequence that minclif built into Cranelift IR and compiles it | minclif, cranelift |
| `.` (`zustc`) | The CLI, and re-exports of the above (for tests and benches). Does not depend on ide or lsp (only the bench lsp/* uses them, as dev-dependencies) | the above (except ide and lsp) |

Each crate's lib.rs re-exports the modules of the lower layers (`pub use zust_syntax::*;` and so on). Inside files, paths are written like
`crate::lexer`. So the same path resolves whichever crate a file is in, and also when self-hosting lays everything out as modules of one crate.

How type checking and the backend are split: acg only records instructions into zust_ir::Recorder (it numbers values, blocks and so on, and remembers the types of values
the same way minclif decides them). check stops there. A build has codegen's lower rebuild the record into minclif's FunctionBuilder in the same order,
then turn it into machine code (minclif creates values and slots inside instructions, so the rebuilding side renumbers them.
`ZUSTC_IR_VERIFY=1` checks that the value types match the record). The output machine code is byte-for-byte the same as before the split.

The only path is **driver2** (`zustc x.rs` uses Cranelift; `--backend=minclif` uses minclif). build, check and the LSP all use driver2.
The first driver (syn + Cranelift, `crates/legacy`) was deleted on 2026-11-16 (it is in the git history).
Self-hosting (tests/selfhost*.sh) combines the sources of base / syntax / sema / ir / typeck / codegen / core and minclif into one file and compiles it with zustc.

## Processing flow (driver2)

The current main path (driver2):

```
src.rs ──srcmap (mod x; files)──▶ macros (macro_rules!) ──▶ flatten modules ──▶ lexer: items + hashes
   ──▶ item summaries (cached, parallel via fork) ──▶ Program (signatures, layouts) ──▶ reachable functions
   ──▶ per function: cached? ── miss ──▶ ast_infer (type inference) → acg (own syntax tree to minclif instruction sequence; -O inlines small functions)
                                        → machine code via Cranelift (zust-clif) or minclif (register allocation) → Blob (parallel via fork)
   ──▶ .o via minclif's ELF writer (includes the panic location table) ──▶ link with wild (skipped if unchanged)
```

| Location | Role |
|---|---|
| `crates/syntax/src/lexer.rs` | Splits top-level items, and hashes the normalized token sequence. Splits `impl` into a header and members |
| `crates/syntax/src/macros.rs` / `srcmap.rs` | Expansion of macro_rules! and include_str!; reading `mod x;` files and mapping lines |
| `crates/syntax/src/parse.rs` / `ast_*.rs` | Own syntax tree, item summaries, type inference, closure analysis, constant evaluation |
| `crates/sema/src/program.rs` | Whole-program tables (signatures, layouts, trait implementations, instances) |
| `crates/typeck/src/acg/` | One-pass lowering from the syntax tree to the instruction sequence (zust_ir::Recorder), and type checking. -O inlines small functions |
| `crates/core/src/driver2.rs` / `cache2.rs` | `Session2`: cache (disk + memory), build / check / workspaces, fork parallelization, writing .o |
| `crates/codegen/src/link.rs` | Extracts the link line from `cc -###`, saves it, and starts the linker directly |
| `crates/minclif` | Instruction recording, register allocation, x86-64 machine code, ELF .o |
| `crates/clif` | Recorded instruction sequence → Cranelift IR → machine code |
| `crates/analyzer/src/lib.rs` | LSP server (holds one `Session2` per document and returns diagnostics from `check`; index of the workspace and std) |
| `crates/ide/src/navigate.rs` / `symbols.rs` | Name resolution for definition, references, hover and completion; symbol lists |
| `src/main.rs` | CLI (build / check / workspace build) |

### Key points of incrementality

(About monomorphization)
- Generic functions and default methods become one instance per requested (function, type arguments).
  The key is "the original function's key + the type arguments (structs by deep hash)".
- Instances are processed with a worklist until a fixed point. The cached Blob of a caller stores its instance references as (original function name, type arguments). So when it is read back, the needed instances are requested again.
- Measured (examples/traits.rs, 25 functions / 11 instances):
  - Editing the body of `total_area<T>` recompiles only its 2 instances.
  - Editing the body of the default method `score` recompiles only the 2 types that use it (Rect, which overrides it, is not affected).
- In check (LSP) too, the "checked" mark includes "the instances this function requested".
  So type errors in generic bodies are reported even when the caller hits the cache.

1. **Changing a callee's body does not recompile the caller.**
   Only the signatures of referenced items go into the key, and the Blob refers to the callee by name (the same idea as blaze's template).
   Only a signature change invalidates the functions that reference it.
2. **Structs are tracked by deep hash.**
   - The deep hash combines the definition hashes of the struct itself and of every struct reachable transitively from its fields. This includes fields reached through references.
   - Structs also go into signature hashes by deep hash.
   - So even a function that does not name `Inner`, like `fn get(o: &Outer) -> i64 { o.inner.b }`, is correctly recompiled when the layout of `Inner` changes (verified).
3. **`impl` blocks are tracked per method.**
   - The lexer splits the `impl X {` header and the members into separate items. The header hash is mixed into each member hash.
   - So editing one method re-parses only that method and recompiles only that method (verified: 1 miss out of 18 functions).
   - Changing a signature recompiles only that method and its callers (2 misses).
   - A method call like `x.len()` enters the reference graph by the last segment of the name (`len`), without looking at types. This counts as referencing `len` of every type, so it is an over-approximation, but it is on the safe side.
4. **Reformatting or editing comments recompiles nothing.**
   The cache hits on everything, and the `.o` is identical, so linking is skipped too.
5. **Unchanged items are not even parsed.**
   Parsing a whole file with syn takes 80ms for 1000 functions (320KB). The own lexer takes only 2.6ms.
6. **Unreachable functions are not parsed, type checked or code generated.**
   As a result, they do not go into the object either.
   A side effect is that type errors inside unreachable functions are not reported (rustc would report them).
7. **Disk usage has an upper bound.**
   Only the entries used in the current build are saved, so old generations disappear automatically. The cache size stays around "the current amount of code".
8. **Memory**
   - Only one function's AST is alive at a time.
   - Cranelift's `Context` and `FunctionBuilderContext` are reused per thread.
   - Incremental builds do not start threads.
   - On cold builds (33 or more item summary misses), the parsing for item summaries runs in parallel, and the ASTs are not brought back.
     Keeping them all made peak RSS 162MB from syn's ASTs alone at 5000 functions. Not bringing them back brought it to 35MB.

## Value representation and ABI (internal)

- **Scalars** (integers, bool, references) are SSA values. References are pointers.
- **Local variables**
  - Scalars whose address is not taken are put in Cranelift `Variable`s (registers).
  - Things referenced by `&x`, and structs, are put in stack slots.
- **Structs**
  - The value is always in memory, and the result of evaluating an expression is "its address".
  - It is copied at let, assignment, argument passing and return (the size is known statically, so it expands to load/store).
  - Arguments: the caller copies into a temporary area and passes its address.
  - Return values: the caller passes the address of an area it allocated as a hidden first argument (sret).
  - Structs cannot be passed by value to or from extern "C" functions (it is an error).
- **Layout**: fields are laid out in declaration order with natural alignment (equivalent to repr(C)).
- **Closures** (`crates/syntax/src/ast_closure.rs`)
  - At the item summary stage, the k-th closure (pre-order) of a body is lifted into the following two (lambda lifting).
    - struct `parent::{closure#k}<parent's type arguments, __C.., __P.., __R>`. The fields are the captures: `*mut T` for a by-reference capture, `T` for `move`.
    - fn `parent::{closure#k}::call(__env: *mut that struct, arguments..) -> __R`.
  - The types of the captures, arguments and return value all go into the struct's type arguments. So the closure's type alone determines the body's instance, and it fits directly into the existing monomorphization and per-instance cache.
  - For the body, the parent item is parsed again, the k-th closure is taken out, made into an ordinary fn and compiled. Captures enter scope as fields of `__env`.
  - A closure that is never called still requests its instance when it is created (to report errors in its body; if unused, `--gc-sections` removes it).
- **Function pointers**: one word holding the function's address. Taken with `func_addr` and called with `call_indirect` (the ABI is the same as an ordinary call).
- **`Box<T>`**: a pointer to the heap (`Box<dyn ..>` is a fat pointer). Auto-deref and conversion to dyn go through the same path as references.
- **drop** (`crates/typeck/src/acg/p6_match_drop.rs`)
  - Local variables and temporaries holding values that need drop are registered as owners, together with a 1-byte drop flag. A move sets the flag to 0, and at scope exit the ones whose flag is 1 are dropped in reverse order (this is correct even when whether a move happens depends on a branch).
  - The drop body is an instance of the prelude's `__exr_drop_in_place::<T>` (drop glue). codegen builds a body that expands only one level per type (call to `impl Drop` → fields / variants / elements → free if Box), and nested types become calls, so expansion stops even for recursive types.
  - The last slot of a vtable is the drop glue of the contained type. Dropping a `Box<dyn Trait>` calls it and then frees.
  - Drop glue is cached per instance. Whether `impl Drop` exists is part of the deep hash, so adding or removing it later rebuilds the functions that use that type.
- **`&dyn Trait`**: 16 bytes of (data pointer, vtable address).
  - A vtable is a sequence of function addresses in the declaration order of the trait's methods, held in the Blob as "a sequence of function IDs".
  - The cache stores them by function name (for an instance, the original function name and type arguments).
  - In the `.o`, they become read-only data deduplicated by content.
  - The vtable of `&dyn Fn(A) -> B` is just the one instance of the closure body.

今の主経路 (driver2):

```
src.rs ──srcmap (mod x; のファイル)──▶ macros (macro_rules!) ──▶ モジュールを平らに ──▶ lexer: アイテム + ハッシュ
   ──▶ 要約 (キャッシュ、fork で並列) ──▶ Program (シグネチャ・レイアウト) ──▶ 到達する関数
   ──▶ 関数ごと: キャッシュ? ── miss ──▶ ast_infer (型推論) → acg (自前の構文木から minclif の命令の列。-O で小さい関数を展開)

```

| 場所 | 役割 |
|---|---|

| `crates/syntax/src/macros.rs` / `srcmap.rs` | macro_rules! の展開・include_str!、`mod x;` のファイルの読み込みと行の対応 |
| `crates/syntax/src/parse.rs` / `ast_*.rs` | 自前の構文木・要約・型推論・クロージャ解析・定数評価 |
| `crates/sema/src/program.rs` | 全体の表 (シグネチャ・レイアウト・trait 実装・インスタンス) |
| `crates/typeck/src/acg/` | 構文木から命令の列 (zust_ir::Recorder) への 1 パスの lowering と型検査。-O で小さい関数をインライン展開 |
| `crates/core/src/driver2.rs` / `cache2.rs` | `Session2`：キャッシュ (ディスク + メモリ)、build / check / ワークスペース、fork の並列化、.o の書き出し |
| `crates/codegen/src/link.rs` | `cc -###` からリンク行を取り出して保存し、リンカを直接起動する |
| `crates/minclif` | 命令の記録・レジスタ割り当て・x86-64 の機械語・ELF の .o |
| `crates/clif` | 記録した命令の列 → Cranelift の IR → 機械語 |
| `crates/analyzer/src/lib.rs` | LSP サーバ (ドキュメントごとに `Session2` を持ち `check` の診断を返す。ワークスペースと std の索引) |
| `crates/ide/src/navigate.rs` / `symbols.rs` | 定義・参照・hover・補完の名前解決と、シンボルの一覧 |
| `src/main.rs` | CLI (build / check / ワークスペースの build) |

### インクリメンタル性の要点

（単相化について）
- ジェネリック関数とデフォルトメソッドは、要求された（関数, 型引数）ごとにインスタンスになる。
  キーは「元の関数のキー + 型引数（struct は deep hash）」。
- インスタンスは作業リストで不動点まで処理する。キャッシュした呼び出し元の Blob には、インスタンス参照を（元の関数名, 型引数）で保存してある。そのため読み戻すと、必要なインスタンスがまた要求される。
- 実測（examples/traits.rs、25 関数 / 11 インスタンス）：
  - `total_area<T>` の本体を編集すると、再コンパイルはその 2 インスタンスだけ。
  - デフォルトメソッド `score` の本体を編集すると、再コンパイルはそれを使う 2 型分だけ（上書きしている Rect は対象外）。
- check（LSP）でも、検査済みの印に「その関数が要求したインスタンス」を入れてある。
  そのため、呼び出し元がキャッシュに当たっても、ジェネリック本体の型エラーは報告される。

1. **callee の本体を変えても caller は再コンパイルされない。**
   キーに入るのは参照先のシグネチャだけで、Blob は callee を名前で参照している（blaze の template と同じ考え方）。
   シグネチャを変えた場合だけ、それを参照している関数が無効になる。
2. **struct は deep hash で追跡する。**
   - deep hash は、その struct 自身と、フィールドから推移的に届く全 struct の定義ハッシュをまとめたもの。参照フィールド経由も含む。
   - シグネチャのハッシュにも、struct は deep hash で入る。
   - そのため、`fn get(o: &Outer) -> i64 { o.inner.b }` のように `Inner` を名前で書いていない関数でも、`Inner` のレイアウトが変われば正しく再コンパイルされる（確認済み）。
3. **`impl` ブロックはメソッド単位で追跡する。**
   - lexer が `impl X {` のヘッダとメンバを別のアイテムに分ける。メンバのハッシュにはヘッダのハッシュを混ぜる。
   - そのため、メソッドを 1 つ編集しても parse し直すのはそのメソッドだけで、再コンパイルもそのメソッドだけ（確認済み：18 関数中 1 miss）。
   - シグネチャを変えた場合は、そのメソッドと呼び出し元だけが再コンパイルされる（2 miss）。
   - `x.len()` のようなメソッド呼び出しは、型を見ずに名前の最後のセグメント（`len`）で参照グラフに入れる。どの型の `len` も参照したことになるので過大近似だが、安全側になる。
4. **整形やコメント編集では何も再コンパイルされない。**
   キャッシュは全ヒットし、`.o` も同一になるのでリンクも省略される。
5. **変わっていないアイテムは parse もしない。**
   ファイル全体を syn で parse すると、1000 関数（320KB）で 80ms かかる。自前 lexer なら 2.6ms で済む。
6. **到達しない関数は parse も型検査もコード生成もしない。**
   その結果、オブジェクトにも入らない。
   その副作用として、到達しない関数の中の型エラーは報告されない（rustc なら報告される）。
7. **ディスク消費に上限がある。**
   保存するのは今回のビルドで使ったエントリだけなので、古い世代は自動的に消える。キャッシュのサイズは「今のコード量」程度に収まる。
8. **メモリ**
   - 同時に生きている AST は常に 1 関数分だけ。
   - Cranelift の `Context` と `FunctionBuilderContext` はスレッドごとに使い回す。
   - インクリメンタル時はスレッドを起動しない。
   - cold 時（要約のミスが 33 件以上）は、要約用の parse を並列にし、AST は持ち帰らない。
     全部保持すると、5000 関数では syn の AST だけでピーク RSS が 162MB になっていた。持ち帰らない形にして 35MB になった。

## 値の表現と ABI（内部用）

- **スカラー**（整数・bool・参照）は SSA 値で表す。参照はポインタ。
- **ローカル変数**
  - アドレスを取られないスカラーは Cranelift の `Variable`（レジスタ）に置く。
  - `&x` で参照されるものと struct はスタックスロットに置く。
- **struct**
  - 値は常にメモリ上にあり、式の評価結果は「そのアドレス」になる。
  - let・代入・引数・return の時点でコピーする（サイズは静的に分かるので、load/store に展開する）。
  - 引数：呼び出し側が一時領域にコピーし、そのアドレスを渡す。
  - 戻り値：呼び出し側が確保した領域のアドレスを、隠れ第 1 引数（sret）で渡す。
  - extern "C" 関数との間で struct を値で受け渡すことはできない（エラーになる）。
- **レイアウト**：宣言順に自然なアラインメントで並べる（repr(C) 相当）。
- **クロージャ**（`crates/syntax/src/ast_closure.rs`）
  - 要約の段階で、本体の k 番目（前順）のクロージャを次の 2 つに持ち上げる（lambda lifting）。
    - struct `親::{closure#k}<親の型引数, __C.., __P.., __R>`。フィールドはキャプチャで、参照キャプチャなら `*mut T`、`move` なら `T`。
    - fn `親::{closure#k}::call(__env: *mut その struct, 引数..) -> __R`。
  - キャプチャ・引数・戻り値の型がすべて struct の型引数に入る。そのためクロージャの型だけで本体のインスタンスが決まり、既存の単相化とインスタンス単位のキャッシュにそのまま乗る。
  - 本体は親のアイテムを parse し直し、k 番目を取り出して普通の fn にしてコンパイルする。キャプチャは `__env` のフィールドとしてスコープに入る。
  - 呼ばれないクロージャも、作った時点でインスタンスを要求する（本体のエラーを報告するため。未使用なら `--gc-sections` で消える）。
- **関数ポインタ**：関数のアドレス 1 語。`func_addr` で取り、`call_indirect` で呼ぶ（ABI は普通の呼び出しと同じ）。
- **`Box<T>`**：ヒープへのポインタ（`Box<dyn ..>` は fat pointer）。参照と同じ経路で自動 deref・dyn への変換をする。
- **drop**（`crates/typeck/src/acg/p6_match_drop.rs`）
  - drop が要る値を持つローカル変数・一時値は、1 byte の drop フラグと一緒に所有者として登録する。ムーブでフラグを 0 にし、スコープの出口でフラグが 1 のものを逆順に drop する（分岐でムーブするかどうかが変わっても正しい）。
  - drop 本体は prelude の `__exr_drop_in_place::<T>` のインスタンス（drop glue）。codegen が型ごとに 1 段だけ展開した本体を作り（`impl Drop` の呼び出し → フィールド / バリアント / 要素 → Box なら free）、入れ子の型は呼び出しにするので、再帰的な型でも展開が止まる。
  - vtable の最後の欄は中身の型の drop glue。`Box<dyn Trait>` の drop はここを呼んでから free する。
  - drop glue はインスタンス単位でキャッシュされる。`impl Drop` の有無は deep hash に入れてあり、後から足し引きしても、その型を使う関数が作り直される。
- **`&dyn Trait`**：(データのポインタ, vtable のアドレス) の 16 byte。
  - vtable は trait のメソッドの宣言順に並べた関数アドレスの列で、Blob に「関数 ID の列」として持つ。
  - キャッシュには関数名（インスタンスなら元の関数名と型引数）で保存する。
  - `.o` では内容で重複を除いた読み取り専用データにする。
  - `&dyn Fn(A) -> B` の vtable は、クロージャ本体のインスタンス 1 個だけ。

# Supported language subset

zustc compiles a subset of Rust. Programs that use std (Vec / String / HashMap / formatting / iterators / Box /
Rc and so on) run on zustc's built-in prelude (`crates/syntax/src/prelude_lib.rs.in`; it is not the real std).
`#![no_std]` programs are also supported.

Correctness is checked by also building the same program with rustc and comparing the results (stdout and exit code)
(`tests/compare.sh` for `examples/*.rs`, `tests/probe.sh` for `tests/probe/*.rs`). For no_std programs, the rustc side is built with libcore only
(`-C panic=abort`).

**Important premise**: there is no borrow checking, mutability checking, move checking, or match exhaustiveness checking (see "Type inference and checking" below). It is a tool
for building programs that already pass rustc quickly, not a replacement for rustc in checking correctness.

## Language

- Items:
  - `fn`
  - `extern "C"` declarations and definitions
  - `struct`: named / tuple / unit
  - `enum`: unit / tuple / struct variants, and discriminants
  - `const`, `static`, `static mut`
  - `use` (names are resolved by the last segment)
  - Crate attributes (`#![no_std]` and so on)
- impl and trait:
  - Inherent `impl`
  - `trait` (required methods and default methods)
  - `impl Trait for S`: struct / enum / primitive types (`impl Tr for u32`)
  - `#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, ..)]`
- Generics:
  - Functions (`<T: A + B>`, `where`, turbofish)
  - struct / enum (`Pair<T>`, `Option<T>`)
  - `impl<T> X<T>`, and self type patterns such as `impl<T> Option<&T>`
  - In all cases, type arguments are inferred at the call site and monomorphized. Lifetimes are erased
  - `impl Trait` in argument position (treated as an anonymous type parameter)
- Closures (`examples/closures.rs`):
  - Captures: by reference (default) and `move` (by value). Nested closures, and bodies containing `self` or method calls
  - `F: Fn(A) -> B` / `FnMut` / `FnOnce` bounds, `impl Fn(A) -> B` arguments, passing `&F` / `&mut F`
  - `impl Fn(A) -> B` in return position (when the tail is a `move` closure that captures only arguments)
  - Stored in struct fields (`struct Button<F: Fn(i64) -> i64> { on_click: F }`, `(self.on_click)(x)`)
  - Parameter and return types are decided in this order: annotation → bound of the callee → usage (type inference of the parent) → type inference of the body
- `dyn Trait` (`examples/dyn_trait.rs`):
  - `&dyn Trait` / `&mut dyn Trait`. Implicit conversion from `&T` (arguments, let, fields, arrays, return values) and `as &dyn Trait`
  - Calls through the vtable to default methods, generic impls (`impl<T> Tr for W<T>`), and impls on primitive types
  - `&dyn Fn(A) -> B` (calls a closure through the vtable)
- Function pointers (`examples/fn_ptr_box.rs`):
  - The `fn(A, B) -> R` type. Using function items as values (arguments, return values, let, struct fields, arrays), `(op.f)(a, b)`
  - Passing a function to `F: Fn(A) -> B` (`apply(double, 5)`, `o.map(double)`)
  - For generic functions, type arguments are decided by turbofish (`id::<i64>`) or by the expected type (`let f: fn(i64) -> i64 = id;`)
  - Converting to `&dyn Fn` / `Box<dyn Fn>` (up to 3 arguments; the prelude's trampoline function `__exr_fnptrN` goes into the vtable)
- `Box<T>` (`examples/fn_ptr_box.rs`):
  - `Box::new(x)` places the value on the heap with libc `malloc`, and drop calls `free`
  - `Box<dyn Trait>` / `Box<dyn Fn(A) -> B>`, auto-deref, `*b`, `&Box<T>` → `&T`, and recursive types such as `Option<Box<Node>>`
- `Vec<T>` / `String` (`examples/vec_string.rs`): written in Rust in the prelude (`crates/syntax/src/prelude_lib.rs.in`). They use libc `realloc` / `free`, and Drop drops the elements before freeing
  - `Vec`: `new` / `with_capacity` / `push` / `pop` / `len` / `is_empty` / `capacity` / `get(_mut)` / `first` / `last` / `insert` / `remove` / `swap_remove` / `swap` / `reverse` / `truncate` / `clear` / `append` / `as_slice` / `as_mut_slice` / `extend_from_slice` / `clone` (`T: Copy`) / `contains` / `==` (`T: PartialEq`) / `sort` (`T: Ord`, insertion sort)
  - `vec![a, b]` / `vec![x; n]`, indexing `v[i]` (panics when out of range), `&v[a..b]`, `for x in &v` / `v.iter_mut()` / `v` (iterating by value)
  - Implicit conversions `&Vec<T>` → `&[T]` and `&String` → `&str` (also to generic `&[T]` arguments)
  - `String`: `new` / `from` / `with_capacity` / `push_str` / `push(char)` (encoded as UTF-8) / `len` / `is_empty` / `as_str` / `as_bytes` / `clear` / `truncate` / `clone` / `==` (between `String`s and with `&str`), `"..".to_string()` / `to_owned()`
  - `==` on `&str` / `&[T]` compares contents
  - Vec / String methods are attached from the prelude only when the type name appears in the code (having a `push` on your own struct is not enough)
- Iterator (`examples/iterators.rs`): the prelude has `trait Iterator { type Item; fn next(..); .. }` and the adapters written in Rust
  - Associated types: `type Item = u32;` (impl) and `Self::Item` / `I::Item` (signatures); type parameters are solved from the constraints `I: Iterator<Item = T>` / `where Self: Iterator<Item = &T>`
  - Your own `impl Iterator for S`, `for x in it` (turned into `while let Some(x) = it.next()`)
  - Producers: `v.iter()` / `iter_mut()` / `into_iter()` (Vec, arrays, slices), `(a..b)` / `(a..=b)` as values, `s.chars()` (decodes UTF-8)
  - Adapters: `map` / `filter` / `filter_map` / `enumerate` / `zip` / `take` / `skip` / `take_while` / `chain` / `copied` / `cloned`
  - Consumers: `collect` (`Vec<_>` / `String`, including the `_` in `collect::<Vec<_>>()` and `let v: Vec<_> = ..`) / `sum` / `product` / `count` / `fold` / `for_each` / `any` / `all` / `find` / `position` / `last` / `nth` / `max` / `min`
  - Closure parameter types are decided by solving the callee's bound (`F: FnMut(Self::Item) -> B`) down to associated types. Type inference also follows associated types (the range in `let s: i64 = (1..=10).sum();` is i64)
  - The prelude's iterator parts are attached only when there is code that creates an iterator and calls adapters or consumers (`v.iter().map(` / `(0..n).sum(` / `impl Iterator` / `.chars()`). They are not attached for just `for x in v.iter()`, just `Option::map`, or just a variable named `count`
- Formatting (`examples/formatting.rs`): `format!` / `print!` / `println!` / `eprint!` / `eprintln!` / `write!` / `writeln!` (to `String` and `fmt::Formatter`)
  - `{}` / `{:?}` / `{:#?}`, positional and named arguments, `{x}` captures, `{{` / `}}`
  - Width, alignment and fill (`{:>8}` / `{:*^9}` / `{:08}` / `{:>w$}`), `+`, `#`, precision (truncation of strings), `x` / `X` / `b` / `o`
  - `impl fmt::Display for S` (`fmt::Result` / `fmt::Formatter<'_>` / `f.pad`) and `x.to_string()`
  - `#[derive(Debug)]` (structs, tuple structs, unit structs, enums, generics). Debug for integers, bool, char, `&str`, String, Vec, arrays, slices, tuples, Option, Result, HashMap
  - The per-type Display / Debug bodies are generated by codegen (`__exr_display::<T>` / `__exr_debug::<T>`). The prelude has only helpers written in Rust
- HashMap (`examples/hashmap.rs`, `examples/text_more.rs`): written in Rust in the prelude (open addressing, linear probing, FNV-1a)
  - `new` / `with_capacity` / `insert` / `get` / `get_mut` / `remove` / `contains_key` / `len` / `is_empty` / `clear` / `m[&k]`
  - `entry(k).or_insert(v)` / `or_insert_with` / `and_modify`
  - `iter` / `iter_mut` / `keys` / `values` / `values_mut` / `into_iter` / `for (k, v) in &m`, `collect::<HashMap<_, _>>()`
  - Keys: integers, bool, char, `&str`, String, and `#[derive(Hash)]` structs / enums / tuples (codegen generates a hash function per type)
  - Iteration order differs from rustc (rustc's is also random, so the examples sort the keys before printing)
- Strings and char (`examples/strings_chars.rs`): if the prelude has `__exr_str_<name>` / `__exr_char_<name>`,
  `s.name(..)` / `c.name(..)` calls it (type inference also uses that signature; a char can be passed to a &str parameter)
  - `to_uppercase` / `to_lowercase` / `replace` / `replacen` / `repeat` / `split("..")` / `split_once` / `strip_prefix` / `strip_suffix` /
    `trim_start` / `trim_end` / `rfind` / `char_indices` / `bytes` / `eq_ignore_ascii_case` / `parse::<integer>()` (Display / Debug of `ParseIntError` are also the same as std)
  - String's `insert` / `insert_str` / `remove` / `pop` / `retain` / `+` / `+=`, `&s[a..b]` (panics if not on a char boundary)
  - char's `is_alphabetic` / `is_numeric` / `is_alphanumeric` / `is_whitespace` / `is_uppercase` / `is_lowercase` / `to_digit` / `is_digit` /
    `to_uppercase` / `to_lowercase` / `len_utf8`, `char::from_digit` / `char::from_u32` / `char::from(u8)`.
    There are no Unicode tables, so it approximates within the ranges of ASCII, Latin-1, Greek, Cyrillic, kana, kanji and Hangul
- More iterators (`examples/iter_vec_more.rs`): `rev` (on Vec, arrays, ranges, chars, and after map / filter / copied / chain; instead of DoubleEndedIterator, each type has `next_back`) /
  `step_by` / `peekable` (`peek` / `next_if`) / `skip_while` / `scan` / `inspect` / `flat_map` / `flatten` (contents are Vec, Option or iterators)
- More Vec / slice: `retain` / `retain_mut` / `dedup` / `dedup_by_key` / `drain(range)` / `split_off` / `resize` / `fill` / `first_mut` / `last_mut` /
  `windows` / `chunks` / `to_vec` / `join` / `concat` (elements are `&str` or String)
- More Option / Result: `expect` / `zip` / `map_or_else` / `or_else` / `and` / `get_or_insert_with` / `insert` / `is_none_or` / `is_ok_and` / `is_err_and` / `map_or`
- clone (`examples/clone_derive.rs`): `#[derive(Clone)]` structs / enums / generics, Box, tuples, arrays, Option, Result, and hand-written `impl Clone`.
  The body is generated per type by codegen (`__exr_clone::<T>`; fields that need no drop are copied, others are cloned field by field)
- Default (`examples/defaults.rs`): `#[derive(Default)]`, hand-written `impl Default`, `Default::default()` / `T::default()` / `i32::default()` / `Vec::default()`,
  struct update syntax `S { a: 1, ..Default::default() }` / `..base`, `unwrap_or_default`, `std::mem::take` / `swap` / `replace` (also for non-Copy types).
  The body is generated per type by codegen (`__exr_default::<T>`: fills with 0, and calls the hand-written impl for fields that have one)
- Collections (`examples/collections.rs`): `HashSet` (on top of HashMap<T, ()>; union, intersection, difference, collect), `BTreeMap` / `BTreeSet` (a Vec kept in key order, with binary search;
  iteration order, `entry().or_insert` / `or_default`, `first_key_value`, `pop_first` and `m[&k]` are the same as std), `VecDeque` (ring buffer; `d[i]`, push / pop at both ends).
  `get("k")` on a map with `&str` / String keys can look up by `&str`, the same as std's Borrow
- `impl Index` / `IndexMut`: `x[i]` becomes `*x.index_mut(i)` if x is a struct with `index` / `index_mut`
- Associated constants (`examples/assoc_consts.rs`): `impl S { const N: usize = 4; }` / trait `const K: u32;` (also with default values). `S::N` / `Self::N` / `T::N` (type arguments), also in array lengths
- Modules (`examples/modules.rs`): `mod m { .. }` within one file (nested, `pub(crate)`, `use self:: / super:: / crate::`, `m::f()` / `m::S` / `m::N`).
  Before lexing, `mod m {` and its matching `}` are replaced with whitespace to flatten them (positions and lines do not change), and name resolution skips the leading module names of a path.
  `#[cfg(test)] mod tests { .. }` is removed
- `macro_rules!` (`examples/macros.rs`): expanded as text before lexing (an expansion fits on 1 line, so later line numbers do not change).
  Fragments expr / ident / ty / literal / tt / block and so on, repetitions `$(..),*` / `$(..)+` / `$(..)?`, recursion, and macros that produce items.
  Expression fragments are embedded wrapped in `( .. )`, so the precedence of `square!(1 + 2)` is the same as Rust
- Operator overloading: `impl Add / Sub / Mul / Div / Rem / Neg / Not / BitAnd / BitOr / BitXor / AddAssign ..`.
  `a + b` becomes `a.add(b)` if the left side is a struct with an `add` method (also right-hand types such as `impl Mul<i32> for V`)
- `&str` methods: `split(char)` / `split_whitespace` / `lines` / `trim*` / `starts_with` / `ends_with` / `contains` / `find` (argument is `&str` or `char`), comparisons such as `<`, and `sort`
- Ordering comparisons (`examples/ordering.rs`, `examples/ordering_impl.rs`, `examples/ordering_inline.rs`):
  - `<` / `<=` / `>` / `>=` on tuples, arrays, slices, `&str`, String, Vec, Option, Result, and `#[derive(PartialOrd, Ord)]` structs / enums (lexicographic; enums by variant discriminant order)
  - Hand-written `impl PartialOrd` / `impl Ord` (also `impl PartialEq` / `impl Eq for S {}`). `<` and sort call them
    - Also sort / sort_unstable / max / min / clamp / BinaryHeap / BTreeMap / BTreeSet / Reverse / bounds `T: Ord` / `T: Eq`, inside tuples and Option, and impls on enums
    - Elements of `==` on arrays, slices, Vec and references also call the hand-written eq
    - collect into `BTreeSet` / `BTreeMap` keeps the later one when equal items follow each other, same as std (insert keeps the earlier key)
  - `cmp` / `partial_cmp` (also on integers), `Ordering` with `reverse` / `then` / `then_with` / `is_lt` and so on, `std::cmp::Reverse`
  - `max` / `min` (also on Ord structs, tuples, String), `std::cmp::max` / `min`
  - `sort` / `sort_by` / `sort_by_key` / `sort_by_cached_key` / `sort_unstable*` (stable merge sort; Vec, arrays, slices, `v[a..b]`), `binary_search` / `binary_search_by` / `binary_search_by_key` (the position returned when equal values are adjacent is also the same as std), `clamp` (integers and Ord types; panics if `lo > hi`), iterator `max` / `min` / `max_by_key` / `min_by_key` / `max_by` / `min_by`
  - `BinaryHeap` (`examples/binary_heap.rs`): `new` / `with_capacity` / `from(vec)` / `collect` / `push` / `pop` / `peek` / `len` / `is_empty` / `clear` / `iter` / `into_iter` / `into_vec` / `into_sorted_vec` / `{:?}`.
    The sift steps are the same as std, so the order of `iter` / `into_vec` / `{:?}` also matches rustc. Min-heap via `Reverse`
  - `BinaryHeap::append` / `extend` (`examples/binary_heap_extend.rs`): the same `rebuild_tail` as std (rebuild everything if many are added, otherwise sift_up one at a time; a different threshold above 2048 elements), so the order after adding also matches
  - `Vec::extend`. The argument can be a Vec, an array, `&v` / `&[..]`, a range, or an iterator (instead of IntoIterator, codegen inserts `into_iter()` / `iter()`; references to elements are added as Copy)
  - The comparison bodies are generated per type by codegen (`__exr_cmp::<T>`; in programs that do not use Box / Vec, they are expanded inline)
- Drop (`examples/drop.rs`, `examples/drop_more.rs`; the drop order is compared with rustc, and valgrind confirms there are no leaks or double frees):
  - `impl Drop for S` (also generic impls), `drop(x)`
  - Drops in reverse declaration order at the end of a scope. This covers scopes exited by return / `?` / break / continue, expression statements that discard a value, `let _ = e`, and old values overwritten by assignment
  - Tracks moves: reading as a value, `self` taken by value, `move` captures, patterns that bind by value (`if let Some(b) = o`), `for x in arr`
  - Temporaries (`make().area()`, `&Box::new(..)`, match scrutinees) are dropped at the end of the statement. Temporaries in a let initializer are extended to the end of the block
  - A move of only a field (`self.top = n.next`) fills the original field with 0 and drops the owner
- Types:
  - Integers (`i8`–`i64`, `u8`–`u64`, `isize`, `usize`), `bool`, `char`, `()`, `!`
  - `&T`, `&mut T`, `*const T`, `*mut T`
  - `[T; N]` (N is a literal or a const), `&[T]`, `&mut [T]`, `&str`
  - Tuples, structs, enums
  - C type aliases such as `core::ffi::c_int`
- Expressions:
  - Arithmetic, bitwise operations, comparisons, short-circuit evaluation, `as`
    - Casts: integer ⇔ char / bool, reference → pointer, pointer ⇔ usize, fieldless enum → integer
  - `let` (also destructuring), assignment, compound assignment
    - The left side can be a local variable, a field, `*p`, `a[i]`, or a static
  - `if` / `match` / `if let` / `while let` / `while` / `loop` / `for` (`break` / `continue` / `return`)
    - Labeled `break 'outer` / `continue 'outer`, `break v` (the value of a `loop`), labeled blocks `'a: { .. break 'a v; .. }`
    - `let PAT = e else { return; };`
  - What `for` can iterate over:
    - `a..b`, `a..=b`, `(a..b).rev()`
    - Arrays and slices (`&xs`, `&mut xs`, by value), and those with `.iter()` / `.iter_mut()` / `.copied()` / `.enumerate()` / `.rev()` applied
  - Construction: struct / tuple / enum / array (`[a, b]`, `[x; N]`)
  - Indexing `a[i]` (panics when out of range), `&a[lo..hi]` (also `..` / `lo..` / `..=hi`)
  - Implicit conversion `&[T; N]` → `&[T]`
  - `==` / `!=`: structs / enums / tuples / arrays are compared structurally. A hand-written `eq` is called if there is one
  - Literals: `"..."` (`&'static str`), `b"..."`, `b'x'`, `'x'`, negative literals
  - `?` (Option / Result)
  - Macros: `panic!` / `unreachable!` / `todo!` / `assert!` / `assert_eq!` / `assert_ne!` / `debug_assert*!` / `matches!`
    - Messages are not formatted
    - `assert_eq!` / `assert_ne!` compare as `==` / `!=` (also Option, Vec, String with `&str`, and so on)
    - Closures inside macro arguments also work (`println!("{:?}", v.iter().map(|x| x * 2).collect::<Vec<_>>())`, `examples/closures_in_macros.rs`).
      Closures are identified by the position of their first `|` (so nodes still correspond when codegen re-parses the macro arguments)
- Patterns:
  - `_`, bindings (`ref` / `mut`), `x @ p`, literals, ranges, `|` (bindings are allowed, as in `A(x) | B(x)`)
  - Slice patterns `[a, b]` / `[first, .., last]` / `[x, rest @ ..]` (arrays, slices, `v[..]`)
  - Variants, structs, tuples, `&p`, nesting, guards
  - Default binding modes when matching on a reference
  - Unit variants such as `None`
- Methods:
  - Auto-deref and auto-ref, UFCS (`S::m(&x)` / `Trait::m(&x)` / `<S as Trait>::m(&x)`)
  - Static dispatch. Lookup order: inherent methods → trait impls → default methods
- Floating point `f32` / `f64`:
  - Arithmetic, `%`, comparisons, `as` casts (conversion to integers saturates, same as rustc), literals `1.5` / `1e-3` / `2.0f32`
  - Methods: `sqrt` / `abs` / `floor` / `ceil` / `round` / `trunc` / `powi` / `powf` / `exp` / `ln` / `sin` / `cos` / `atan2` / `hypot` / `mul_add` / `max` / `min` (ignore NaN) / `total_cmp` / `is_nan` / `to_bits` and so on (transcendental functions use libm)
  - Constants: `f64::MAX` / `EPSILON` / `NAN` / `INFINITY` / `consts::PI` and so on. Path calls such as `f64::sqrt(x)`
  - Formatting uses the same digits as rustc: shortest representation (the shortest digits that round-trip to the same value; `{:?}` uses the `1e-7` form when the exponent is -5 or less or 16 or more), `{:.N}` (round-half-to-even from the exact decimal expansion). Decimal conversion is done exactly with base-1e9 multi-precision arithmetic
  - `"1.5".parse::<f64>()` (strtod, `ParseFloatError`)
  - The 6000 lines of `examples/float_fuzz.rs` (Display / Debug / `{:.N}` / parse of random bit patterns) match rustc
- 128-bit integers `i128` / `u128`:
  - Arithmetic, comparisons, shifts and bitwise operations use Cranelift's I128 (arguments and return values use 2 registers, the same as SysV, via `enable_llvm_abi_extensions`)
  - Division, remainder, conversion to and from floating point (rounded once), formatting (`{}` / `{:x}` / `{:b}` / width and so on), and `parse` are prelude functions
  - `checked_*` / `wrapping_*` / `pow` / `count_ones` / `MAX` / `MIN`, HashMap keys, derive
  - The randomized check in `examples/int128.rs` (3000 pairs of arithmetic, shifts and comparisons) matches rustc
- Other:
  - Integer `overflowing_*` / `checked_pow` / `saturating_pow` / `rem_euclid` / `div_euclid` / `next_power_of_two` / `leading_ones` / `isqrt` / `from_str_radix`
  - Calling primitive methods in function form, such as `i32::pow(2, 10)`
  - `From` impls and `.into()` (`from` of the expected type; `String::from` for String, a cast for numbers)
  - `vec![v; n]` with non-Copy elements (cloned and laid out), `concat` of `Vec<Vec<T>>`, `collect::<String>()` with `&str` / `String` elements
  - `partition` / `rposition`, `collect::<Option<Vec<T>>>()` / `collect::<Result<Vec<T>, E>>()`, type inference for method turbofish
  - `String::from_utf8` / `std::str::from_utf8` (validation and the display of `Utf8Error` are the same as std), the `trim_matches` family (pattern is &str / char / closure), `rev()` on `split` / `lines` / `split_whitespace`
  - `Rc` (`clone` / `strong_count` / `ptr_eq`; no weak references), `RefCell` (`borrow` / `borrow_mut` only return references and do not check borrows), `Cell`

  - Format `{:e}` / `{:E}` (also with precision), `{:w$}` / `{:.p$}` / `{:.*}` taking width and precision from arguments, combinations of width and type such as `{:12e}`
